- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a small upward bias for early period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged high; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual decline.
- Mean reversion is evident: model frequently overpredicts mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; reduce forecast slope toward end of horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.6 → -0.2 → +0.4), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not just price history.
